title: Automated generation and surrogate modeling of 3D urban wind simulation based on physics-informed graph neural networks: a two-stage framework
abstract: The spatial configurations of buildings under strong wind conditions influence building energy efficiency and the surrounding microclimate. Full-scale and high-resolution simulations are severely constrained by substantial computational costs and time requirements. This study proposes a two-stage framework that integrates AI-based generative design with a physics-informed surrogate model for the rapid prediction of 3D urban wind fields. The framework automatically generates 3D community-scale building layouts using datasets from three Chinese cities. A dynamic-prioritization physics-informed graph neural network is then developed to predict wind pressure and velocity distributions. A T-shaped sampling strategy is introduced to preserve spatial fidelity while reducing computational costs. Evaluated on six 3D cases, the model achieves NRMSEs of 8.91% for pressure and 12.26% for velocity relative to CFD benchmarks, with a speedup of over two orders of magnitude. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of combining AI-generative design with physics-informed learning for efficient urban planning and microclimate evaluation.

title: An adaptive industrial large language model for mechanical fault diagnosis under variable operating conditions
abstract: Under variable operating conditions, mechanical vibration signals exhibit strong nonlinearity and time-varying characteristics. Traditional signal processing and deep learning methods struggle to extract stable fault features, posing challenges to early equipment fault detection and health management. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the Variable Operating Condition Large Language Model (VOC-LLM). The model builds a multidimensional vibration feature fusion module to embed time-domain statistical features, time–frequency domain entropy features and nonlinear dynamic features into the Transformer semantic space. It encodes variable-speed features to capture time-varying signal dependencies and designs lightweight adaptation for the large language model (LLM). This adaptation achieves efficient domain alignment with industrial scenarios while preserving pre-trained knowledge. The model deeply couples mechanical fault semantics with model inference logic to realize interpretable quantitative assessment of fault severity. Tested on both laboratory and industrial platforms, VOC-LLM significantly outperforms mainstream advanced methods. It accurately identifies equipment faults of varying severity levels, providing a practical and interpretable solution for predictive maintenance of industrial equipment.

title: Hamiltonian-based energy shaping with attention-augmented fourier neural operators for adaptive torque control in ankle rehabilitation robot
abstract: In rehabilitation robotics, control of energy flow is not merely a stability requirement but a therapeutic tool that shapes the quality and safety of human-robot interaction (HRI). The precise modulation of potential and kinetic energy within the coupled human–robot system governs how assistance is provided, how disturbances are rejected, and how patient effort is encouraged. Energy shaping approaches enable the controller to sculpt an artificial energy landscape anchored at a prescribed reference posture, so that restorative torques emerge naturally from the gradient of the shaped potential and disturbance-rich interactions are regulated within bounded, passive operating limits. This study presents a novel deep learning-based energy shaping framework for torque control in a three-degree-of-freedom (DOF) ankle rehabilitation robot. The proposed method is rooted in port-Hamiltonian mechanics. It employs interconnection and damping assignment-passivity-based control (IDA-PBC) to shape the energy landscape of the system, promoting practical stability and safe patient interaction. To address the limitations of static or heuristic energy shaping, we introduce a physics-informed data-driven approach in which the potential energy function is dynamically constructed through an Attention-Augmented Fourier Neural Operator (AFNO). This architecture learns mappings from spatiotemporal sensor data, including joint kinematics and interaction torques, to optimal shaping parameters that define the control energy field. The control strategy was experimentally validated on an ankle rehabilitation robot with ten healthy subjects (eight male, two female, aged 25–43), performing controlled movements across dorsiflexion/plantarflexion, inversion/eversion, and abduction/adduction. Experimental data confirmed that the shaped potential energy fields successfully guided joint trajectories toward the prescribed reference posture under disturbance-rich interaction conditions, while maintaining passivity and minimizing unnecessary energy expenditure.

title: Physics-Informed Multi-Fidelity Neural Network with Fourier features for three-dimensional flow field reconstruction in planar cascades
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional flow field reconstruction in planar cascades is crucial for the aerodynamic design of turbomachinery. Existing methods for obtaining flow field data, including experimental measurements and numerical simulations, have limitations such as long cycles and high computational resource consumption. Driven by the development of artificial intelligence, data-driven modeling has emerged as a new paradigm for cascade flow field prediction. However, single models rely on large amounts of high-fidelity (HF) data, significantly increasing the modeling costs. Although multi-fidelity learning can improve the prediction accuracy by fusing multi-fidelity data, purely data-driven knowledge transfer however exhibits insufficient accuracy in predicting complex flows and is prone to overfitting. To address these issues, this study proposes a Physics-Informed Multi-Fidelity Neural Network with Fourier features (fPIMFNN) that integrates physics constrained multi-fidelity learning. The framework implements a multi-fidelity collaboration network for cross-fidelity knowledge transfer, embeds the Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) equations as physical constraints to ensure prediction consistency, and conducts Fourier feature embedding to strengthen the capture of multi-scale flow features. Experimental results on a transonic cascade demonstrate that the proposed fPIMFNN outperforms various competitors, thus providing a data-efficient solution for complex three-dimensional flow field modeling.

title: Data-driven inverse design of aperiodic metastructures for tailored vibration isolation using evolutionary active learning
abstract: Traditional metamaterials often struggle to adaptively manage broadband random disturbances and specific frequency resonances for complex equipment under time-varying conditions due to their fixed bandgaps. To address this, we propose a physically embedded evolutionary active learning framework for the inverse customization and intelligent reconfiguration of non-periodic flexible metastructures using small-sample data. Specifically, a hierarchical decoupling strategy—training a Deep Neural Network (DNN) solely for local constitutive mappings and coupling it with physical transfer matrices—is proposed to fundamentally overcome the “curse of dimensionality” inherent in global designs. Furthermore, an active learning-driven closed-loop feedback mechanism is integrated with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) algorithm. Ablation studies confirm that, by dynamically updating the surrogate model through targeted physical validations, this closed-loop strategy achieves superior convergence efficiency and computational efficiency compared to traditional optimization approaches. Results indicate a coefficient of determination (R2) exceeding 0.98 on the validation set, with relative errors kept within 2.0%. The framework demonstrates a hierarchical “global customization-individual reconfiguration” capability. In the passive customization phase, the Pareto front autonomously provides a broad coverage of aperiodic designs to meet diverse isolation requirements. Subsequently, active reconfiguration was validated on two typical configurations selected from the Pareto front. For Configuration 1, current control significantly expanded the tunable ranges: attenuation constants to [0.39, 1.49], starting frequencies to [14.98, 41.90] Hz, and effective bandwidths to [21.74, 68.29] Hz. For Configuration 2, stiffness reconfiguration maintained high attenuation levels [0.51, 1.41] while enabling flexible adjustment of starting frequencies [14.03, 38.57] Hz and bandwidths [16.89, 47.98] Hz. Finally, wave mechanics and experiments confirm that this data-driven approach provides a comprehensive solution for intelligent vibration isolation in complex engineering.

title: MCMC with adaptive principal-component transformation: rotation-invariant universal samplers for bayesian structural system identification
abstract: Over decades, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods have been widely studied, with a typical application being the quantification of posterior uncertainties in Bayesian system identification of structural dynamic models. To address the issue of excessively low sampling efficiency in generic MCMC methods when applied to specific problems, researchers developed several MCMC algorithms that integrate trainable neural networks to replace and enhance their critical components. Later, meta-learning MCMC methods emerged to reduce training time. However, they require considerable similarity between test and training tasks, while their sampling efficiency is constrained by trade-off-simplified network designs. This paper proposes the Adaptive Principal-Component (PC) Meta-learning Stochastic Gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (APM-SGHMC) algorithm. It adaptively rotates coordinate axes in the parameter space to align with the PC directions of the current posterior samples, ensuring rotation-invariance of sampling performance with respect to the posterior distribution. By incorporating translation-invariance, scale-invariance, and rotation-invariance in a unified framework, APM-SGHMC enables universal samplers to acquire generalizable knowledge across diverse Bayesian system identification tasks using minimalistic tasks while eliminating the constraints imposed by network design trade-offs on sampling efficiency. Practical feasibility issues are also addressed. Two Bayesian system identification case studies demonstrate its effectiveness and universality: our method overcomes the case-by-case limitations of traditional data-driven approaches, achieving zero-shot generalization across structurally distinct models without retraining and maintaining consistent superior performance across all scenarios.

title: Physics-informed event-frame fusion learning paradigm for high dynamic range 3D industrial metrology
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) optical metrology is essential for manufacturing quality and lifecycle management in intelligent industrial manufacturing. However, significant reflectance variations in industrial environments present a challenging problem for high dynamic range (HDR) optical 3D metrology. Traditional frame-based fringe projection profilometry achieves precise phase reconstruction on texture-rich surfaces but is limited by the inherently low dynamic range of frame-based cameras in ultra-HDR scenarios. Event-driven FPP offers robust HDR compatibility (≥120 dB), yet its event-based output, incompatible with conventional vision techniques, struggles to recover fine geometric details. To address this, we propose PhyHDR-DL, a physics-informed deep multimodal learning framework that integrates event streams and frame images for industrial 3D measurement. Unlike data-driven methods, PhyHDR-DL embeds two physics-informed priors into an end-to-end deep learning architecture (PhyHDR-Net): (1) an HDR simulation algorithm generating physically consistent training pairs under extreme illumination gradients, and (2) an enhanced sinusoidal-cosine component generation method extracting physics-aware features for event stream learning. Experiments show that PhyHDR-Net, trained on diffuse reflection scenes, enables ultra-high-resolution inference in unseen HDR industrial scenarios, delivering accurate and detailed phase reconstruction. Compared to data-driven approaches, PhyHDR-DL reduces phase reconstruction errors in complex HDR scenes, with mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) decreasing by 65.9 % and 11.05 %, respectively. This physics- informed fusion of frame and event data offers a novel solution to HDR 3D metrology challenges in intelligent manufacturing.

title: Human-inspired zero-shot semantic segmentation of construction point clouds based on adaptive observation and MLLM reasoning
abstract: Semantic segmentation of as-built point cloud data is a cornerstone of construction digital twins. However, existing 3D AI models are often confined to specific, well-annotated datasets and suffer from poor generalization in complex construction environments. This paper proposes a human-inspired zero-shot framework for construction scene segmentation, featuring a modular architecture comprising: (1) an action module for hybrid pre-segmentation, (2) an observation module for dynamic viewpoint adjustment, and (3) an analysis module leveraging multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for semantic interpretation. Without task-specific training, the proposed method achieved over 85 % weighted IoU on real-world construction datasets, drastically outperforming state-of-the-art open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding methods (less than 40 % weighted IoU). This superior performance highlights the approach’s potential for downstream applications such as progress monitoring, quality inspection, and human-robot collaboration. Furthermore, it establishes a new paradigm for domain-adaptive 3D scene segmentation, effectively overcoming limitations related to data scarcity and cross-domain generalization.

title: Physics-informed graph neural networks for sim-to-real structural response prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of structural dynamic responses under complex environmental conditions remains a fundamental challenge in engineering, primarily due to nonlinear coupling effects and the inherent limitations of both traditional numerical simulations and purely data-driven approaches. Conventional physics-informed neural networks embed physical constraints through loss function penalties, which may be violated during inference. To address this limitation, this paper presents a Physics-Informed Graph Convolutional Network (PIGCN) framework that implements hard physical constraints by directly encoding structural dynamics equations into the network architecture. Specifically, the mass and stiffness matrices are embedded into the graph adjacency structure to weight inter-node connections according to their mechanical significance, and physics-informed transfer functions derived from the structural dynamics governing equation are introduced to replace conventional activation functions, ensuring that every forward pass inherently satisfies fundamental physical principles. The effectiveness of the PIGCN framework is demonstrated through simulation-to-real cross-domain prediction experiments on two representative structural systems: flexible cables under platform excitation and spatial steel frames under multiple dynamic loadings. The model achieves R2 values up to 0.979 for acceleration predictions and consistently exceeds 0.924 for strain predictions, significantly outperforming conventional deep learning architectures. Notably, the model exhibits strong cross-domain generalization, accurately predicting real-world measurements using only simulation-trained data. This study establishes a unified and physically consistent deep learning paradigm for structural response prediction, offering substantial potential for intelligent health monitoring in marine and civil engineering applications.

title: A physics-informed digital design framework to enhance freeze–thaw durability of engineered concrete: A case study on basalt fiber concrete
abstract: The performance degradation of concrete under freeze–thaw cycles (FTC) is a critical durability challenge in cold-region engineering. Traditional empirical methods lack generalizability, while high-fidelity physical models are hampered by difficulties in parameter identification and high computational cost. However, purely data-driven approaches frequently yield unreliable extrapolations due to their black-box nature and lack of physical consistency. To address this, this study develops a parametric physics-embedded neural network (PPENN) framework integrated with a customized multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm, thereby forming an autonomous design system to enhance the freeze–thaw durability of basalt fiber concrete (BFC). The core innovation involves embedding a damage constitutive equation into the PPENN, enabling direct mapping from mix proportions to physical parameters. The trained model generates physically consistent predictions that are fed into the optimization algorithm to efficiently explore the Pareto frontier between economic cost and durability. Results show: (1) The model achieves higher accuracy on sparse/noisy data, with ablation studies confirming the importance of the physical decoding module; (2) The system successfully identifies complex cost–performance trade-offs and outputs corresponding mix designs, with the enhanced optimizer outperforming standard benchmarks in solution uniformity; and (3) Independent univariate freeze–thaw tests validate the system’s logic and feasibility. This work provides an efficient tool for frost-resistant BFC design and establishes a generalizable, performance-based framework for intelligent material prediction and development.

title: When sensing meets computational Intelligence: A comprehensive survey on pipeline damage detection and localization
abstract: Intelligent computational methods are increasingly central to pipeline damage detection and localization, enabling a transition from periodic inspection toward continuous, data-driven structural health monitoring. This review provides an integrated and critical synthesis of machine learning, deep learning, and advanced computational approaches for pipeline monitoring, examined in direct relation to pipeline failure mechanisms, sensing data characteristics, and localization requirements. Modern sensing modalities (e.g., acoustic, fiber-optic, pressure, and ultrasonic measurements) are examined primarily as inputs to intelligent computational frameworks for pipeline damage detection and localization under nonstationary conditions. Beyond methodological developments, the review critically examines implementation challenges that limit real-world deployment, including sensitivity to noise, scarcity of labeled fault data, generalization across pipeline assets, computational scalability, and integration with operational constraints. Emerging paradigms such as physics-informed and hybrid modeling, transfer learning, generative data augmentation, edge computing, and autonomous monitoring are discussed as enablers for reliable and scalable deployment. Unlike prior reviews that treat sensing and analytics in isolation, this work unifies physical failure processes, sensing strategies, and intelligent computation within a single engineering framework, highlighting pathways for translating advanced analytics into actionable decision-support tools for inspection planning, risk assessment, and maintenance of large-scale pipeline infrastructure.

title: Immutable AI: A blockchain-based MLOps framework for auditable solar forecasting and anomaly logging
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are increasingly adopted in Industrial IoT (IIoT) and renewable energy systems, yet conventional MLOps pipelines still provide limited guarantees regarding the integrity, traceability, and post-hoc verifiability of model execution. This limitation is especially relevant in solar-plant operations, where forecast-driven alarms may influence maintenance prioritization and forensic analysis after incidents. In this work, we define Immutable AI as an MLOps pattern in which model artifacts, inference inputs, and selected outputs are cryptographically fingerprinted off-chain and anchored on-chain to create a tamper-evident audit trail. Based on this concept, we propose a hybrid framework that combines an LSTM model for photovoltaic power forecasting with Ethereum smart contracts for audit registration. The framework hashes serialized model artifacts, input snapshots, and inference records, and links them to MLflow run metadata to support version-aware verification. The prototype is assessed using a real-world photovoltaic dataset containing approximately 682,000 raw measurements across multiple installations, with detailed forecasting experiments conducted on a high-quality reference installation after preprocessing. The forecasting module achieves an RMSE of 0.1567 kW on the selected test set, while the blockchain layer demonstrates feasible anomaly-event notarization on Sepolia under a hash-only storage strategy. Rather than claiming full predictive-maintenance validation, the paper positions the contribution as an auditable forecasting and anomaly-logging framework that strengthens integrity, provenance, and reproducibility for maintenance assurance workflows. The study also formalizes the threat model, discusses privacy and trust assumptions, and analyzes latency, cost, and scalability trade-offs relevant to industrial deployment.

title: Applications, challenges, recommendations, and future directions of additive manufacturing with transfer learning
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive discussion of how transfer learning (TL) techniques can be integrated to enhance process monitoring in additive manufacturing (AM), with the aim of transforming the field. AM has emerged as a powerful approach to create complex geometries and facilitate rapid prototyping, addressing critical drawbacks of traditional manufacturing such as material wastage, extended production timelines, high tooling costs, and intricate post-processing. Although data-driven monitoring during the AM process has improved AM’s reliability and productivity, they continue to face significant challenges due to the inherently dynamic nature of the process, limited data availability, and increased post-processing costs. TL, a subset of machine learning that transfers knowledge from data-rich source domains to data-scarce targets, offers a promising solution. This paper begins by providing an overview of machine learning development in AM. It highlights the challenges faced within the AM domain, the limitations of AM modeling, and the importance of high-level monitoring of AM processes. It then outlines strategies for applying TL to tackle these issues and offers comprehensive insights into integrating TL frameworks in the context of AM. The review identifies three key AM trends in the TL application: anomaly detection, process monitoring, and geometric deviation modeling. Moreover, it examines data acquisition methods, dominant pre-trained architectures, and evaluation approaches within the scope of integrating TL in AM. Finally, we identify seven main challenges associated with TL implementation in AM and offer practical guidelines to address these challenges, thereby proposing viable paths for future AM advancement.

title: Noise-aware optimization in nominally identical manufacturing and measuring systems for high-throughput parallel workflows
abstract: Device-to-device variability in experimental noise critically impacts reproducibility, especially in automated, high-throughput systems like additive manufacturing farms. While manageable in small labs, such variability can escalate into serious risks at larger scales, such as architectural 3D printing, where noise may cause structural or economic failures. This contribution presents a noise-aware decision-making algorithm that quantifies and models device-specific noise profiles to manage variability adaptively. It uses distributional analysis and pairwise divergence metrics with clustering to choose between single-device and robust multi-device Bayesian optimization strategies. Unlike conventional methods that assume homogeneous devices or generic robustness, this framework explicitly leverages inter-device differences to enhance performance, reproducibility, and efficiency. An experimental case study involving three nominally identical 3D printers (same brand, model, and close serial numbers) demonstrates reduced redundancy, lower resource usage, and improved reliability. Overall, this framework establishes a paradigm for precision- and resource-aware optimization in scalable, automated experimental platforms.

title: LST-MADNet: Learnable scattering transform network for multi-modal time-series anomaly detection in industrial manufacturing systems
abstract: Robust anomaly detection in heterogeneous, multi-channel time-series data is essential in modern manufacturing systems. Traditional rule-based methods and many existing AI-driven approaches often fall short in capturing the complex temporal, spectral, and cross-modal patterns inherent in such data, frequently struggling with varying sampling frequencies and the inability to identify anomalies arising from inter-sensor correlations. To address this, we propose LST-MADNet, a novel neural network architecture designed for multi-modal time-series anomaly detection. At its core is LSTL-1D, a neural layer that replaces the fixed wavelet filters of conventional scattering transform networks (STNs) with parameterized wavelets. This enables the extraction of invariant time-frequency representations suitable for industrial anomaly detection. LSTL-1D serves as the foundational stage of LSTN, a single-channel anomaly detection model. We extend LSTN to LST-MADNet using various fusion schemes to integrate data from multiple sensors, treating each distinct frequency as a separate modality and capturing critical cross-channel correlations that may indicate anomalies. We validate the proposed framework on a real-world industrial dataset collecting time-series data from three modalities in a robotic screwing process. Our results demonstrate superior performance compared to state-of-the-art deep learning baselines. It is observed that the network is capable of effectively adapting its frequency focus depending on the spectral content of the time-series data, extracting representations that are well-suited for anomaly detection. The introduction of a learnable scattering-based representation and a modular, fusion-oriented architecture represents a significant advancement toward scalable monitoring systems in industrial manufacturing.

title: Physics-informed interaction attention enhanced residual network for reliable HVAC fault diagnosis under severe class imbalance
abstract: Reliable fault diagnosis under severely imbalanced data distributions remains a fundamental challenge in engineering systems. Conventional deep models often exhibit degraded minority-class recognition and unstable decision boundaries when training samples are highly skewed toward normal conditions. To address this issue, we propose a physics-informed interaction attention and efficient channel attention enhanced ResNet (PIA-ECA-ResNet), where PIA introduces a soft structural prior to model cross-sensor interactions among chiller operating variables through a learnable coupling matrix and sample-adaptive gating, and ECA provides lightweight channel recalibration to strengthen robust feature abstraction under data scarcity. To further improve diagnostic reliability for easily confused minority fault categories, a decoupled two-stage classification framework is developed to separate anomaly detection from fine-grained fault identification. Experiments on a benchmark chiller dataset with imbalance ratios up to 200:1 demonstrate that the proposed architecture consistently outperforms standard residual networks and conventional baselines. Under extreme imbalance, the model achieves 91.72 % accuracy and improves macro-F1 to 92.1 %, indicating enhanced class-balanced performance and reduced missed detections. With the two-stage strategy, overall accuracy increases to 93.6 %, while recall for refrigerant-related faults improves substantially, effectively mitigating false-negative risks. These results demonstrate that embedding physics-informed interaction modeling into attention-enhanced residual architectures provides a robust and generalizable solution for fault diagnosis under severe class imbalance, offering improved reliability for practical engineering decision support.

title: A collaborative deformation prediction method for multiple monitoring points of concrete gravity dams: physics-informed feature selection and multi-task deep learning model
abstract: Dam deformation serves as a critical response indicator reflecting the structural safety status of a dam body. Its spatiotemporal evolution characteristics are of great significance for the operational safety assessment and risk early warning of dams. However, existing deformation prediction methods mostly focus on single monitoring points and fail to effectively capture the spatiotemporal correlations among different monitoring points. Even multi-point modeling is often constrained by issues such as insufficient representation of physical knowledge, feature redundancy, and inadequate characterization of spatiotemporal collaborative relationships. To address these problems, this paper proposes a physics-informed feature selection and multi-task deep learning model. Firstly, a finite element model is constructed. Combined with Multi-Output Support Vector Regression and the Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimizer, joint inversion of material parameters for multiple monitoring points is performed to derive physically informed driving features. Secondly, a two-stage feature selection strategy is established. Robust preliminary feature screening via BorutaShap and SHapley Additive exPlanations-based incremental feature selection are adopted to refine key driving information and obtain the optimal feature subset for each monitoring point. Subsequently, a multi-task learning-based collaborative prediction model named Parallel Multi-branch Temporal Convolutional Network- Dynamic Cross-Channel Convolutional Block Attention Module-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (PMTCN–DCCBAM–BiLSTM) is constructed. The parallel multi-branch temporal convolutional network independently extracts the local temporal features of each monitoring point. The dynamic cross-channel convolutional block attention module is introduced to enhance the response of key driving factors, and the bidirectional long short-term memory network is used to capture the global spatiotemporal evolution patterns of dam deformation, thereby achieving accurate collaborative prediction of multi-point deformation. Finally, validation is performed using monitoring data from a concrete dam. The results show that the proposed model reduces the mean squared error (MSE) by an average of 94.37% and increases the coefficient of determination (R2) by an average of 9.47%. The proposed method enables multi-point collaborative prediction and constructs a unified knowledge representation framework integrating physical mechanisms, spatial relationships and temporal response laws. It provides a generalizable methodological foundation for identification of dam response patterns, anomaly attribution analysis and decision support for safety monitoring.

title: A physics-informed transformer with relaxation mechanism for robust tire force estimation across diverse road conditions
abstract: Accurate and robust tire force estimation across diverse road conditions is essential for vehicle motion control and safety. However, estimation performance is often degraded by transient dynamic mismatch, tire-road nonlinearity, and varying road conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Physics-Informed Transformer (PIT) framework integrated with a shallow Bayesian Neural Network (BNN). Unlike standard rigid physical constraints, a slack-relaxation mechanism is introduced into the dynamic residual to provide a structured relaxation for transient inconsistency between the estimated tire-force-induced dynamics and measured vehicle responses. The network is trained using a composite loss that explicitly enforces dynamic, kinematic, and wheel-speed constraints. Furthermore, the Bayesian output head performs Monte Carlo sampling to construct a prior distribution, which is then refined online through physics-residual-based updating to obtain a physics-fused posterior for enhanced robustness and physical consistency. Experimental diverse road conditions demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more accurate and robust tire force estimation than the benchmark methods under ice-snow, asphalt, and composite road conditions.

title: High-performance modeling of conventional and active hydrostatic/hybrid bearings: Applying coupled physics-informed neural networks (PINN) for reducing data volume and time costs
abstract: The study addresses the issue of improving the performance of fluid film bearing models, in particular hydrostatic and hybrid bearings, both conventional and adjustable. Data-driven models typically outperform numerical ones, but also require large amount of data and time for training. Applying physically-informed neural networks (PINN) for this purpose partly reduces the required amount of data and time costs when considering fairly simple bearing designs, mainly hydrodynamic ones. However, the problem is still acute for hydrostatic/hybrid bearings, especially having active design, due to a higher number of degrees of freedom. The study proposes an approach based on utilizing a combination of separate PINNs to reduce the costs of building surrogate dynamic nonlinear bearing models while maintaining the performance advantages. A relatively simple PINN-based model of a basic plain bearing is utilized at the first stage of the modeling process to calculate the hydrodynamic lubricant pressure distribution. At the subsequent stage, this distribution is modified by another PINN-based model taking into account the lubricant pressure in hydrostatic recesses. The proposed division of models reduces the dimensionality of the training dataset and shows an advantage over the numerical model in time required for solving a set of test rotor dynamic problems by approximately an order of magnitude with little difference in accuracy. The results are useful for design procedures for high-performance rotor supports, including active supports, reducing the time required for modeling, as well as for synthesizing such models.

title: AutoSurrogate: An LLM-driven multi-agent framework for autonomous construction of deep learning surrogate models in subsurface flow
abstract: High-fidelity numerical simulation of subsurface flow is computationally intensive, especially for many-query tasks such as uncertainty quantification and data assimilation. Deep learning (DL) surrogates can significantly accelerate forward simulations, yet constructing them requires substantial machine learning (ML) expertise, from architecture design to hyperparameter tuning, that most domain scientists do not possess. Furthermore, the process is predominantly manual and relies heavily on heuristic choices. This gap remains a key barrier to the broader adoption of DL surrogate techniques. In this work, we present AutoSurrogate , a large-language-model-driven multi-agent framework that empowers practitioners without ML expertise to build high-quality surrogates for subsurface flow problems through natural-language instructions. Given simulation data and optional preferences, four specialized agents collaboratively execute data profiling, architecture selection from a model zoo, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization (HPO), model training, and quality assessment against user-specified thresholds. The system also handles common failure modes autonomously, including restarting training with adjusted configurations when numerical instabilities occur and switching to alternative architectures when predictive accuracy falls short of targets. In our setting, a single natural-language sentence can be sufficient to produce a deployment-ready surrogate model, with minimal human intervention required at any intermediate stage. We demonstrate the utility of AutoSurrogate on two representative subsurface flow problems, including a 3D geological carbon storage case and a 2D underground hydrogen storage case, where surrogate models are constructed to map geological properties (e.g., permeability, porosity) to spatio-temporal pressure and saturation fields. Without any manual tuning, AutoSurrogate is able to outperform a range of baseline models and domain-agnostic AutoML methods. The results demonstrate strong potential of the AutoSurrogate framework for practical deployment in scientific and engineering applications.

title: A market-rule-informed neural network for efficient imbalance electricity price forecasting
abstract: Accurate and efficient imbalance electricity price forecasting is critical for industrial energy trading in balancing markets. Battery assets and automated trading systems require forecasts with limited computational resources and near-real-time speed. The imbalance price is formed through known market rules that aggregate various market signals into the final market outcome. For accurate price forecasting, this raises a methodological question: can future prices be sufficiently forecast from only lagged prices, or are raw market signals needed? This paper argues for the latter and proposes a market-rule-informed neural network (MRINN) that embeds market rules into the latent space. By embedding these rules, the proposed model preserves raw signal information while avoiding the need to relearn known market rules, leading to a compact model with faster training and inference. We further examine operational robustness under delayed or missing signals and characterize performance scaling across input length and forecasting horizon. Our case studies provide empirical evidence that the proposed MRINN improves forecasting accuracy by 8% compared with the best lagged-price-only baseline, while reducing the number of trainable parameters by around 90% relative to raw-signal neural baselines. The data and code are open-sourced at https://github.com/runyao-yu/MRINN .

title: A synergistic framework combining explainable AI and multiphysical simulation for uncovering process–structure relationships in mask electrolyte jet machining
abstract:
A significant challenge in advanced manufacturing is the deep, physically-grounded understanding of complex process–structure relationships, which is essential for robust process optimization and control. This study introduces a novel “Predict-Explain-Corroborate” framework designed to address this challenge within the context of Mask Electrolyte Jet Machining (MEJM). The novelty of this work lies not in the individual deployment of predictive modeling, Explainable AI (XAI), or physical simulation, but in their synergistic integration into a structured methodology to uncover and validate complex physical mechanisms. title: A physics-informed neural network approach for random vibration analysis of train-bridge system via probability density evolution equation
abstract: To address the high computational cost and numerical stability constraints of conventional finite-difference solvers for the probability density evolution equation (PDEE) in train-bridge system (TBS) stochastic vibration analysis, this study proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based framework. A train-bridge coupled dynamic model is first established, and the governing equation of motion and the corresponding PDEE are derived. These two equations serve fundamentally different purposes, with the equation of motion governing the deterministic system response and the PDEE describing the probability evolution of that response. Then, the PDEE, together with initial and boundary conditions, is embedded into the PINN loss via automatic differentiation, enabling a mesh-free solution for the time-dependent probability density function (PDF). Taking the stochastic dynamic response of a high-speed railway bridge as the target, the proposed method is validated against conventional probability density evolution method (PDEM) benchmark solutions. Numerical investigations under varying train speeds and random train-parameter conditions demonstrate that the method achieves high accuracy and stability in solving the PDEE. The main contributions are fourfold: (i) a physics-informed framework embedding the generalized PDEE into the network loss for mesh-free PDF evolution; (ii) a 42.7 % reduction in PDEE-solving cost versus finite-difference PDEM with maintained statistical accuracy; (iii) robustness across train speeds of 260–340 km/h and load coefficient of variation (CV) of 0.08–0.16; and (iv) accurate capture of non-Gaussian features and time-varying evolution for infrastructure reliability assessment.

title: A hybrid physics-informed neural network-crossformer framework for inversion of reservoir parameters in large-scale gas storage flow systems
abstract: Large-scale underground natural gas storage (UNGS) faces challenges such as drastic changes in injection-withdrawal rates and periodic cycling, which hinder traditional machine learning methods by reducing pressure prediction accuracy and reservoir parameter inversion reliability. To address this, this paper proposes a hybrid framework combining physics-informed neural networks with Crossformer model for high-accuracy transient pressure prediction in UNGS during the pressure build-up period. The model utilizes the preceding pressure and gas injection–withdrawal rates as input, and reservoir pressure as output. The cubic spline interpolation is utilized to handle data sparsity, and a moving window method is used to calculate pressure derivatives. By explicitly embedding the residuals of the reservoir flow governing equations into the loss function, the model is guided to learn patterns consistent with reservoir physics. A weighted abrupt change-point loss mechanism is introduced to enhance the model’s detection of abrupt changes. The whale optimization algorithm is employed for network and hyperparameters tuning. The framework achieves an early-stage mean squared error of 6.49 × 10-9 and a prediction accuracy of 99.98% after inverse normalization. The application in the real case of the Hutubi UNGS shows that the initial formation pressure is 31.78 MPa and the permeability is 11.64 mD.

title: LLM-guided hybrid control and meta-optimization for multi-BESS voltage regulation in distribution networks
abstract: With high penetration of renewable energy, prediction errors, measurement noise, and operating condition variations jointly lead to significant voltage fluctuations in distribution networks. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) provides an effective solution for coordinated voltage regulation in distribution networks with battery energy storage systems (BESS), yet its performance is highly sensitive to hyperparameter configurations. Conventional approaches typically reduce multi-dimensional performance metrics to a single scalar objective, making it difficult to balance multiple operational requirements such as voltage security and battery lifetime, and often leading to performance degradation under complex operating conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hierarchical LLM-guided hybrid meta-optimization framework (H2M2O), consisting of a decision-making layer for real-time coordinated control and an adaptation layer for online policy evolution. At the decision-making layer, a hybrid policy integrating MASAC and MATD3 is developed, where gated fusion and bidirectional distillation are employed to jointly enhance robustness and control precision. At the adaptation layer, Bayesian optimization and heavy-tailed stochastic exploration are combined to generate diverse candidate solutions, while a large language model (LLM) is utilized to interpret multi-dimensional performance metrics and adapt hyperparameters accordingly. Simulation results on the IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate that, compared with fixed-parameter baselines, the proposed method improves cumulative return by 33% while reducing voltage deviation and state-of-charge (SoC) fluctuation by 28.1% and 31.1%, respectively. Moreover, it exhibits superior robustness and generalization compared with model predictive control (MPC) and Bayesian optimization approaches under varying disturbance conditions.

title: A dual-retrieval augmented Multimodal Large Language Model framework for automatic post-earthquake building safety evaluation
abstract: Rapid post-earthquake building safety evaluation is critical for disaster response, infrastructure rehabilitation, and public safety. However, traditional manual inspections remain labor-intensive, time-consuming, and hazardous. While current task-specific inspection models excel at damage detection yet fall short in reasoning, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer semantic reasoning but lack the domain-specific seismic engineering knowledge required for standard-compliant safety evaluation. To address this, this study proposes SeisMLLM, a novel dual-path retrieval-augmented MLLM framework that bridges visual damage perception and expert-level safety evaluation. To enable this framework, this work constructs SeisMLLM-1k, the first case-level multi-view dataset comprising 3,856 images across 1,306 building cases from 17 global earthquakes, with annotations strictly grounded in standard protocols, e.g., ATC-20-1 Field Manual: Postearthquake Safety Evaluation of Buildings. In this study, SeisMLLM explicitly decouples visual perception from safety judgment via a domain-finetuned MLLM, and grounds the reasoning process through a dual-path retrieval strategy encompassing both historical damage cases and the regulatory logic of ATC-20-1. An ATC-20-1 compliant assessment report is ultimately generated via chain-of-thought reasoning. Experimental results demonstrate that SeisMLLM effectively mitigates critical failure modes of general-purpose MLLMs, outperforming representative open-source baselines by an average of 38.5 percentage points in safety evaluation accuracy, and achieving a leading accuracy of 66.13%. Overall, SeisMLLM transforms black-box predictions into an interpretable, standard-compliant solution for automated building safety evaluation.

title: A physics-informed dynamic transmission error-driven inversion network for few-shot gear spalling severity identification
abstract: Gear transmission systems may develop tooth surface spalling of varying severity during service. Beyond detecting the presence of a fault, identifying spalling severity provides more targeted information for condition assessment and maintenance. However, measured data covering different spalling severity levels are usually scarce in practical applications, which limits the training of data-driven severity identification models. Existing data generation methods face challenges in terms of physical fidelity and virtual-real consistency. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a physics-informed dynamic transmission error-driven inversion network (PI-DTEN) for few-shot gear spalling severity identification. First, by embedding a gear dynamic model into the neural network, PI-DTEN directly uses reconstructed in-situ dynamic transmission error (DTE) signals to drive the inversion of key dynamic parameters. Since DTE characterizes the in-situ relative motion error between the driving and driven gears, it is more directly related to the gear meshing process than housing vibration responses. Therefore, using reconstructed in-situ DTE as the observation can reduce the dependence on housing vibration signals and alleviate the influence of transfer-path attenuation and structural noise during parameter inversion. Second, a physically meaningful multi-constraint hybrid loss function, a physical normalization strategy, and a resonance-inspired spectral calibration strategy are integrated to improve the reliability of the identified parameters and the virtual-real consistency of the generated data. Finally, using the reliable physical parameters identified by PI-DTEN, additional virtual DTE samples for a healthy reference state and three prescribed spalling levels of 2.5%, 5%, and 7.5% are forward-generated and combined with the limited measured samples to train a standard 1D-CNN model. Experimental results on a gearbox test rig show that the proposed method achieves an average classification accuracy of 92.2%, indicating its effectiveness in supporting few-shot gear spalling severity identification.

title: Physics-informed analytical intelligence framework for mechanism-driven decision support of tool wear in smart machining systems
abstract: Tool wear critically governs the reliability, quality, and economic efficiency of machining systems; however, existing modeling approaches remain predominantly prediction-oriented, empirically dependent, and insufficiently capable of extracting mechanism-driven knowledge for intelligent manufacturing decision support. This study develops a physics-informed analytical intelligence framework that transforms fundamental wear mechanisms into interpretable computational reasoning for smart machining systems. The framework integrates abrasion, adhesion, and diffusion within a unified force–temperature-coupled analytical formulation, establishing explicit relationships between wear evolution, material properties, thermo-mechanical fields, and process parameters. Unlike conventional approaches that primarily focus on numerical wear prediction, the proposed framework enables analytical interpretation of mechanism dominance, transition behaviour, and parameter sensitivity without experimental calibration. A gradient-based sensitivity analysis further converts the analytical formulation into decision-relevant knowledge, allowing systematic evaluation of tool–material compatibility and machining conditions during early-stage process planning. The framework is evaluated across four representative machining scenarios and experimentally validated using both uncoated and coated tools. The predicted mechanism transitions and coating-dependent behaviors exhibit consistent agreement with observed wear patterns, demonstrating the capability of the proposed framework to provide physics-based decision support beyond conventional wear prediction. By integrating cutting mechanics, thermo-physical material attributes, and multi-mechanism wear evolution into a unified analytical intelligence structure, this work establishes a foundation for interpretable and data-efficient digital manufacturing systems, enabling knowledge-driven tool selection and process planning in smart machining environments.

title: Dual-path physics-informed heterogeneous information fusion for axial piston pump health assessment in construction machinery
abstract: Reliable health assessment of hydraulic power components is essential for autonomous construction machinery. As the core power component, the health of axial piston pumps directly impacts the safety of automated process. However, traditional single-source data-driven methods are limited by incomplete information and vulnerable to sensor malfunctions or data loss. To address this, we propose a dual-path physics-informed heterogeneous information fusion (DP-PIHIF) framework, which consists of a Virtual Health Indicator (VHI) path and a Physical Health Indicator (PHI) path, integrating high-frequency vibration and relatively low-frequency physical data. In the VHI path, multi-domain vibration features are extracted and compressed using a Variational Autoencoder to characterize dynamic fault signatures. In the PHI path, a Physics-Informed Transformer is developed to infer interpretable leakage-related coefficients from multi-sensor hydraulic measurements, with physical consistency enforced through a volumetric flow loss model. The resulting VHI and PHI representations are integrated using an adaptive heterogeneous fusion module with dynamic weight allocation, followed by a multi-task learning scheme for simultaneous health state classification and ordinal health-level regression. Experimental results show superior assessment accuracy and regression stability, outperforming single-source baselines. This indicates the promising potential of the proposed framework for remote health assessment, which may support the predictive maintenance and operational continuity in autonomous construction machinery.

title: 3D CSFM: Cross-domain adaptation of visual foundation models for 3D seismic fault segmentation
abstract: Three-dimensional seismic fault segmentation is a knowledge-intensive task in subsurface structural interpretation and hydrocarbon exploration. Yet scarce field annotations limit robustness across acquisition and processing conditions, while unlabeled seismic data lack the scale and diversity needed to train a fault-oriented foundation model from scratch. We therefore propose 3D CSFM, a cross-domain framework that adapts a pretrained vision foundation model (VFM) to 3D fault segmentation through three components. Inspired by the directional structures of seismic volumes, the Bidirectional 3D Feature Adaptation Encoder (Bi3DA-Encoder) employs complementary spatial-view and depth-view pathways to model within-slice fault extension and cross-slice offset variations, respectively, while embedding lightweight depthwise-separable 3D adapters into the pretrained 2D vision encoder to transform planar visual priors into direction-aware 3D fault representations without extensive fine-tuning. The Spatial Context-Aware Decoder (SCA-Decoder) uses multiscale 3D context aggregation and deep supervision to reconstruct continuous fault structures and delineate weak boundaries. To bridge the synthetic-to-field domain gap, cross-domain collaborative training couples a seismic-structure-aware VFM branch comprising the Bi3DA-Encoder and SCA-Decoder with a local-detail-sensitive 3D convolutional branch, dynamically fuses the branches’ complementary predictions to generate target-domain supervision, and applies consistency and discrepancy regularization to reduce pseudo-label error accumulation and confirmation bias. Trained with synthetic labels and unlabeled field data, 3D CSFM quantitatively outperforms baselines on the synthetic validation set and labeled Thebe field data. Qualitative results on F3 and the unseen Kerry and Poseidon surveys support its effectiveness on these specific surveys. The framework enables annotation-efficient seismic fault interpretation and VFM adaptation in knowledge-intensive geophysical workflows.

title: LLM-augmented progressive search for efficient multi-robot task planning
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate potential in task planning, with a small portion of that work dedicated to multi-robot collaboration tasks. However, existing studies focus on using multiple LLMs engaging in collaborative dialogue to attempt to find good plans, while the efficiency of these plans remains uncertain due to hallucinations and inaccuracies exhibited by LLMs. To cope with this issue, we propose the Retrieval-augmented Progressive Search with LLMs (RePS-LLM), which is the first to introduce LLMs into search algorithms for reliably finding efficient action plans in multi-robot collaboration. More specifically, the LLM policy is assisted by retrieval-augmented generation to progressively add actions, biasing the search toward estimating the values of more promising actions. In addition, our method proposes a group selection strategy to constrain the progressive action selection, improving search efficiency by ensuring that the LLM adds feasible coordinating actions. Experimental evaluations indicate that RePS-LLM surpasses state-of-the-art LLM planning frameworks, yielding an average 46% increase in success rate and a 15% reduction in steps with more than 10 robots.
